agents.label: Design QA
agents.summary: The CX Retail Exchange UK microsite is functional and contains most required elements, but presents as a template-assembled page rather than a designed one. Brand color inconsistencies (cyan/pink CTAs instead of the configured accent #FF5A36), an uncontrolled type scale mixing Raleway with no evidence of Archivo/Inter, and visibly uneven spacing throughout the page all undercut the professional tone the event warrants. Mobile stacking is broadly intact but several sections lose hierarchy and touch targets feel cramped.

findings.location: Layout & grid · Featured article / two-column split section, desktop (~400px from top)
findings.issue: The left image column and right text column are not vertically aligned at their tops — the image bleeds lower than the text block, and the two halves sit at different vertical anchors, breaking the grid row.
findings.recommendation: Apply `align-items: stretch` or `align-items: start` consistently to the flex/grid row container so both columns share the same top edge.
findings.fix_prompt: In the two-column section that contains the event photo on the left and 'Powering Personalisation' body text on the right, add `align-items: start` to the parent row container and ensure both columns use the same top padding value (e.g. 48px) so they share a common top edge.

findings.location: Layout & grid · Past Sponsors grid, desktop
findings.issue: Sponsor logos are sized inconsistently — some logos (e.g. 'Labs', 'Profound') render at very large text sizes while others (e.g. 'SIERRA', 'Simple AI') use actual image assets, creating a visually jagged, non-grid-aligned row.
findings.recommendation: Constrain all sponsor logos to a uniform container height (e.g. 48px) with object-fit: contain and center-align them vertically within a consistent grid column.
findings.fix_prompt: In the 'Our Past Sponsors' section, set a fixed height of 48px and width of auto on every sponsor logo `` element, add `object-fit: contain` and `display: block; margin: auto` so all logos are uniformly sized and vertically centered within their grid cells.

findings.location: Layout & grid · Photo Gallery section, desktop (near bottom)
findings.issue: The photo grid mixes a wide left image with a narrow right column of two stacked images, and the 'Request your invite' CTA card floats without clear grid anchoring — its right edge does not align to the section container boundary.
findings.recommendation: Define a 3 or 4-column CSS grid for the gallery and place the CTA card as a proper grid cell so all edges align to the grid tracks.
findings.fix_prompt: Convert the Photo Gallery section to a CSS grid with `grid-template-columns: 2fr 1fr 1fr` and place the CTA card in the third column spanning both rows so its edges align to the grid, removing any absolute or ad-hoc positioning.

findings.issue: The brand config specifies Archivo for headings and Inter for body text. The page CSS loads and applies Raleway for both headings and body copy. No evidence of Archivo or Inter is present in the stylesheet.
findings.recommendation: Import Archivo and Inter from Google Fonts and update the CSS custom properties: `--primary-font: 'Archivo', sans-serif` and `--secondary-font: 'Inter', sans-serif`.
findings.fix_prompt: In the `<style data-dynamic>` block, replace the @import for Raleway with `@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Archivo:wght@400;700;800&family=Inter:wght@400;600&display=swap')` and update `--primary-font: 'Archivo', sans-serif` and `--secondary-font: 'Inter', sans-serif`.

findings.location: Typography · Hero section, desktop — event date/location line
findings.issue: The date and location text ('30 June – 1 July 2027, London, UK') renders at a size that appears nearly equal to the value-proposition subheadline below it, flattening the heading hierarchy in the most critical section of the page.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate the date/location line by using a smaller weight or size (e.g. 14–16px, regular weight) relative to the event name (48px) and subheadline (20–24px).
findings.fix_prompt: For the element with class `.cta-event-date` inside the hero, set `font-size: 15px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase` to visually subordinate it to the event name and value proposition headlines.

findings.location: Typography · Body content sections (e.g. 'Secure Your Place' banner, 'Wondering what's in store?' section)
findings.issue: Heading sizes throughout the mid-page sections appear to use 4–5 different arbitrary sizes that do not map to the defined type scale [12,14,16,20,24,32,48,64]px — several section headings look visually equivalent to body text, destroying hierarchy.
findings.recommendation: Audit all heading elements and assign sizes strictly from the brand type scale: H1=48px, H2=32px, H3=24px, H4=20px, body=16px, captions=14px.
findings.fix_prompt: Add a global style rule: `h1 { font-size: 48px } h2 { font-size: 32px } h3 { font-size: 24px } h4 { font-size: 20px } p, li { font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.6 } .caption, small { font-size: 14px }` and remove all inline font-size overrides that deviate from these values.

findings.issue: Speaker name and job title are rendered in nearly the same font size and weight, making it hard to distinguish name from title at a glance.
findings.recommendation: Set speaker name to 16px/700 weight and title to 13px/400 weight in a muted colour (#555) to create clear name-to-title separation.
findings.fix_prompt: In the speaker card component, apply `font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; color: #1A1A1A` to the name element and `font-size: 13px; font-weight: 400; color: #555555` to the title/company element.

findings.location: Spacing & rhythm · Mid-page sections (Benefits, Sponsorship, Article rows), desktop
findings.issue: Vertical spacing between sections is inconsistent — some sections feel tightly packed (the 'Benefits of Attending' and 'Benefits of Sponsoring' headings have almost no top margin from the preceding video strip), while others have large unexplained voids (the quote/testimonial pink section).
findings.recommendation: Apply a consistent inter-section gap of 64px or 96px (from the brand spacing scale) using section padding, and remove ad-hoc margins that create irregular rhythm.
findings.fix_prompt: Add a global CSS rule: `.page-section { padding-top: 64px; padding-bottom: 64px; }` and apply the class `page-section` to every major section container, removing existing inconsistent inline padding/margin overrides.

findings.location: Spacing & rhythm · 'Secure Your Place' pink CTA banner, desktop
findings.issue: The banner text is cramped against the left edge with insufficient left padding, while the CTA button on the right has excessive surrounding whitespace — padding is asymmetric and not drawn from the spacing scale.
findings.recommendation: Set symmetric horizontal padding of 48px on both sides of the banner container and ensure the button has equal top/bottom padding (13px per the existing btn rule).
findings.fix_prompt: On the 'Secure Your Place' banner container element, set `padding: 32px 48px` and ensure the inner flexbox has `align-items: center; justify-content: space-between` so text and button are evenly distributed with consistent padding on both sides.

findings.issue: The gap between speaker cards is noticeably smaller than the gap between the speaker grid and the 'View Past Speakers' CTA button below it — proximity grouping is inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Set card-to-card gap to 24px and card-grid-to-CTA gap to 32px so the CTA reads as belonging to the section but with a clear hierarchical separation.
findings.fix_prompt: On the speakers grid container, set `gap: 24px; margin-bottom: 32px` and ensure the 'View Past Speakers' button sits directly below with `margin-top: 0` (relying on the grid's margin-bottom for spacing).

findings.issue: There are three CTA buttons in the hero ('Request Your Invite', 'Download Post Event Report', 'Become a Sponsor') rendered at similar visual weights. The primary registration CTA should be dominant; the secondary and tertiary CTAs compete with it equally.
findings.recommendation: Style 'Request Your Invite' as the filled accent button (#FF5A36 background, white text), 'Download Post Event Report' as a ghost/outline button, and 'Become a Sponsor' as a text link or tertiary ghost to establish clear CTA priority.
findings.fix_prompt: In the hero CTA row, add class `btn-primary` only to the 'Request Your Invite' button with `background-color: #FF5A36; color: #ffffff; border: none`, change 'Download Post Event Report' to `btn-outline` with `border: 2px solid #ffffff; background: transparent; color: #ffffff`, and change 'Become a Sponsor' to a plain text link styled `color: #ffffff; text-decoration: underline; font-weight: 600`.

findings.location: Visual hierarchy · Mid-page CTA buttons (multiple sections)
findings.issue: CTAs throughout the page use cyan (#00c9ff), pink (#ff3fb1), and magenta colours that are not in the brand palette. These arbitrary colours create a fairground effect and dilute the visual weight hierarchy.
findings.recommendation: Replace all CTA button colours with the brand accent #FF5A36 for primary actions and #0A2540 for secondary actions, removing the cyan and pink values from the CSS variables.
findings.fix_prompt: In the `:root` CSS block, change `--primary-color: #FF5A36`, `--primary-color-hover: #e04a28`, `--secondary-color: #0A2540`, `--secondary-color-hover: #0d3360`. Remove the cyan and pink values entirely so all buttons inherit the correct brand palette.

findings.location: Visual hierarchy · Article/blog card row near bottom, desktop
findings.issue: 'READ NOW' links on the three article cards are styled identically to section headings in weight, making it ambiguous which text is a heading and which is a CTA.
findings.recommendation: Style 'READ NOW' as a small caps or underlined link at 13–14px rather than a bold block that matches heading weight.
findings.fix_prompt: On all `.read-now` or equivalent CTA link elements in the article cards, apply `font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: #FF5A36; text-decoration: underline` to differentiate them from headings.

findings.issue: Buttons across the page use at least five different background colours (cyan, pink, magenta, dark navy, white/outline) with no apparent rule governing which colour is used where. This is not a consistent component system.
findings.recommendation: Define a maximum of three button variants (primary, secondary, ghost) and enforce them globally, as noted in the Visual Hierarchy axis.
findings.fix_prompt: Audit every `<a class='btn'>` and `<button>` element on the page and replace colour-specific inline styles or ad-hoc classes with one of three canonical classes: `btn-primary` (accent fill), `btn-secondary` (dark fill), or `btn-ghost` (transparent with border). Delete any CSS classes not mapping to these three variants.

findings.issue: The page alternates between white, light grey, dark gradient, pink/magenta, and a gradient purple-to-pink background — at least 6 distinct background treatments with no discernible system. This creates a garish patchwork appearance.
findings.recommendation: Limit background treatments to three: white (#FFFFFF), light grey (#F5F6F7), and brand dark (#0A2540). Reserve gradient or accent backgrounds for one hero section only.
findings.fix_prompt: Replace all section `background` declarations that use pink, magenta, cyan, or purple gradient values with either `background: #ffffff`, `background: #F5F6F7`, or `background: #0A2540` depending on whether the section needs light, subtle, or dark treatment. Remove the pink and gradient background values entirely.

findings.location: Consistency · Speaker cards vs. article cards, desktop
findings.issue: Speaker cards use circular portrait crops while article cards use rectangular image crops — this is acceptable — but the card container border-radius, shadow, and padding differ between speaker cards and sponsor cards in a way that makes them look like they came from different component libraries.
findings.recommendation: Define a single card token (e.g. border-radius: 8px, box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.08), padding: 16px) and apply it uniformly to all card-type components.
findings.fix_prompt: Create a CSS class `.event-card { border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.08); padding: 16px; background: #ffffff; }` and apply it to all card elements (speaker cards, article cards, sponsor cards), removing conflicting individual card styles.

findings.location: Responsive integrity · Past Sponsors grid, mobile
findings.issue: On mobile, sponsor logos that are rendered as large text strings ('Labs', 'Profound') wrap awkwardly and appear disproportionately large relative to the image-based logos beside them, disrupting the sponsor row layout.
findings.recommendation: Ensure all sponsor entries are image assets at a consistent container height (40px) so they stack cleanly in a 2- or 3-column grid on mobile.
findings.fix_prompt:
In the sponsors section, wrap each sponsor in a `
` for mobile (using a 2-column flex-wrap layout) and enforce `max-height: 40px; width: auto; object-fit: contain` on every sponsor ``, converting any text-only sponsors to logo image assets.

findings.location: Responsive integrity · 'Benefits of Attending' and 'Benefits of Sponsoring' sections, mobile
findings.issue: On mobile these two sections stack vertically as expected, but both heading texts ('Benefits of Attending a CX Retail Exchange' and 'Benefits of Sponsoring a CX Retail Exchange') are cut to approximately the same visual weight as the body text below — there is no mobile-specific heading size reduction, causing both to feel like the same level.
findings.recommendation: Ensure H2/H3 elements in these sections still render visibly larger than body text on mobile — a minimum of 24px for section headings vs. 15-16px for body text.
findings.fix_prompt: Add a responsive rule: `@media (max-width: 768px) { .benefits-section h2 { font-size: 24px; line-height: 1.3; margin-bottom: 16px; } .benefits-section p { font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.6; } }` replacing `.benefits-section` with the actual section class name.

findings.issue: On mobile the hero CTA buttons stack vertically which is correct, but the 'Download Post Event Report' button text appears to be close to wrapping or is slightly cut at the right edge at 390px width.
findings.recommendation: Ensure hero buttons on mobile have a max-width of 100% and padding that allows the longest button label to fit on one line, or allow the label to wrap gracefully to two lines.
findings.fix_prompt: Add `@media (max-width: 480px) { .hero .btn { width: 100%; max-width: 100%; white-space: normal; text-align: center; padding: 12px 16px; } }` to ensure all hero CTA buttons are full-width and text wraps cleanly on narrow screens.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Hero section — text over background image, desktop and mobile
findings.issue: The event name and supporting text in the hero are rendered over a photographic background image without a sufficiently dark scrim. In areas where the image is light (faces, bright clothing), the white text becomes difficult to read. The axe-core report confirms 17 nodes with contrast failures, and `.btn-primary` elements are among them.
findings.recommendation: Add a semi-transparent dark overlay to the hero image container: `background: linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(10,37,64,0.65) 0%, rgba(10,37,64,0.45) 100%)` so all text achieves minimum 4.5:1 contrast against the image.
findings.fix_prompt: On the hero section's image container, add a pseudo-element or overlay div: `.hero-overlay { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: rgba(10, 37, 64, 0.60); z-index: 1; }` and ensure all hero text and button elements have `position: relative; z-index: 2` so they render above the scrim.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Primary CTA buttons, global (e.g. 'Request Your Invite', 'Find Out More')
findings.issue: The cyan (#00c9ff) primary button colour on a white background and white text on cyan both fail WCAG AA contrast (the axe-core report confirms .btn-primary contrast failures). This makes CTA text unreadable for users with low vision.
findings.recommendation: Change button background to brand accent #FF5A36 with white text — this pairing achieves approximately 3.8:1 which is borderline; alternatively use #0A2540 (dark navy) background with white text which achieves >10:1.
findings.fix_prompt: In the CSS `:root` block, set `--primary-color: #0A2540` and `--primary-color-hover: #FF5A36`. Update `.btn-primary { background-color: var(--primary-color); color: #ffffff; }` and `.btn-primary:hover { background-color: var(--primary-color-hover); color: #ffffff; }` to ensure all primary buttons meet WCAG AA contrast.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Testimonial / quote section — pink/magenta gradient background, desktop
findings.issue: The quote text and attribution are rendered in white over a bright pink-to-magenta gradient. The lighter magenta areas of the gradient likely fall below 4.5:1 contrast ratio for normal-weight body text.
findings.recommendation: Darken the gradient stops so the lightest point is no lighter than #C2185B equivalent, or add a semi-transparent dark overlay, or change text to a dark colour (#1A1A1A) if the background is lightened.
findings.fix_prompt: On the testimonial section, change the background to `background: linear-gradient(135deg, #8B0057 0%, #B0003A 100%)` so the gradient stays dark enough for white text to achieve at least 4.5:1 contrast throughout. Then verify with a contrast checker before publishing.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Footer — small print and links
findings.issue: Footer text (Privacy Policy, Cookie Policy, T&Cs links and contact details) appears to be rendered at approximately 11–12px in a mid-grey colour over a dark background. At this size WCAG requires enhanced contrast (7:1 for AAA, or ensure at least 4.5:1 at AA for small text).
findings.recommendation: Increase footer small text to a minimum of 14px and ensure colour contrast of footer links against the footer background is at least 4.5:1.
findings.fix_prompt: In the footer CSS, set `footer .footer-links a, footer .footer-small-text { font-size: 14px; color: #d0d0d0; }` and `footer { background-color: #0A2540; }` to ensure the #d0d0d0-on-#0A2540 pairing meets WCAG AA contrast for small text.

agents.summary: The page has a functioning Event schema and reasonable meta description copy, but the title tag is critically short and keyword-thin (21 chars, no year, no location signal), which hurts click-through for intent-specific queries. The meta description is nearly three times the safe length at 449 characters, meaning Google will truncate it unpredictably and the opening value proposition is buried. The H1 avoids the event name entirely, creating a keyword coherence gap between headline, title, and metadata that dilutes topical relevance signals.

findings.issue: Title is only 21 characters and omits the event year (2027), city (London), and primary topic keywords ('retail CX conference'). It provides no differentiation from a brand name lookup and will not match high-value discovery queries such as 'retail customer experience conference UK 2027' or 'CX event London 2027'.

findings.issue: The meta description is 449 characters — approximately three times the ~155-character display limit. Google will auto-truncate at a sentence boundary that may exclude the most compelling differentiators (AI-driven CX, invitation-only, roundtables). The same oversized text is also used for og:description, which will truncate poorly on social cards.
findings.recommendation: Reduce to 150–160 characters. Lead with the strongest differentiator (invitation-only, London, 2027), include 'retail CX' and one unique benefit to drive the click.
findings.fix_prompt: Rewrite the meta description to between 150 and 160 characters. Open with the event's clearest differentiator (invitation-only, senior retail CX leaders, London 2027), include the keywords 'retail CX', 'loyalty', and 'AI', and end with an implicit CTA. No exclamation marks or unverifiable superlatives.

findings.issue: The H1 ('The Exclusive, Invitation-only Event for CX, CS, & Digital Retail Leaders in the UK') does not contain the event name 'CX Retail Exchange UK' or the year/city. This breaks keyword coherence between the title tag, schema name field, and on-page headline, weakening topical authority signals and making it harder for Google to confirm what the page is definitively about.
findings.recommendation: Revise the H1 to include the event name and, if design permits, the year and location. The descriptor phrase can follow as a subheading. Example H1: 'CX Retail Exchange UK 2027' with an H2 subhead describing the audience.
findings.fix_prompt: Update the H1 so it contains the exact event name 'CX Retail Exchange UK' and the year '2027'. Move the current H1 text ('The Exclusive, Invitation-only Event for CX, CS, & Digital Retail Leaders in the UK') to an H2 or a styled paragraph directly beneath the H1. findings.issue: Both highPrice and lowPrice are empty strings in the AggregateOffer block. An empty string is not a valid schema value; it can cause Google's Rich Results validator to flag a price-related warning and suppress price display in event rich results.
findings.recommendation: If pricing is not yet confirmed, remove the highPrice and lowPrice properties entirely rather than publishing empty strings. Set offerCount to the correct number of offer types or remove it if unknown.
findings.fix_prompt: In the Event JSON-LD, remove the 'highPrice' and 'lowPrice' keys from the AggregateOffer object if their values are empty strings. Also correct 'offerCount' to reflect the actual number of offer tiers, or remove it. Do not add invented prices.

findings.issue: The offer availability value is set to 'https://www.cxnetwork.com/events-customer-experience-exchange-retail-uk/InStock', which is a page URL rather than the required schema.org vocabulary value (e.g., 'https://schema.org/InStock'). This will fail structured data validation.
findings.recommendation: Replace the availability value with the correct schema.org URI: 'https://schema.org/InStock'.
findings.fix_prompt: In the Event JSON-LD offers block, change the 'availability' value from 'https://www.cxnetwork.com/events-customer-experience-exchange-retail-uk/InStock' to 'https://schema.org/InStock'.

findings.issue: The event @id is 'https://www.iqpc.com#event', which points to the IQPC corporate domain rather than the canonical URL of this specific event page. This breaks entity disambiguation and prevents Google from correctly associating structured data with this URL.
findings.recommendation: Set @id to the canonical event URL with a fragment: 'https://www.cxnetwork.com/events-customer-experience-exchange-retail-uk#event'.
findings.fix_prompt: In the Event JSON-LD, change the '@id' value to 'https://www.cxnetwork.com/events-customer-experience-exchange-retail-uk#event' to match the canonical page URL.

findings.location: Event JSON-LD — location.url and location address fields
findings.issue: The venue URL, streetAddress, and postalCode are all empty strings. While the city is provided, absence of a full address and venue name (beyond 'London, UK') reduces the richness of event rich results and may cause a venue-related warning in Search Console.
findings.recommendation: Add the specific venue name and address if available on the page. If not stated on the page, remove the empty string fields rather than publishing blank properties.
findings.fix_prompt: In the Event JSON-LD location block, remove any keys whose values are empty strings ('url', 'streetAddress', 'postalCode', 'telephone'). If the venue name and address are visible anywhere in the page content, populate them accurately; do not invent values.

findings.issue: The WebSite schema block sets 'url' to 'https://www.iqpc.com' but the page lives on 'https://www.cxnetwork.com'. This cross-domain mismatch can confuse Google's entity graph and incorrectly associates the website entity with IQPC rather than CX Network.
findings.recommendation: Update the WebSite JSON-LD 'url' and '@id' to 'https://www.cxnetwork.com' and rename the entity 'name' to 'CX Network' consistently.
findings.fix_prompt: In the WebSite JSON-LD block, change 'url' to 'https://www.cxnetwork.com' and '@id' to 'https://www.cxnetwork.com#website'. Ensure 'name' reads 'CX Network' (not 'CX Retail Exchange UK') to reflect the site-level entity rather than the individual event.

findings.issue: No robots meta tag is present (value is null in the deterministic check). While the site is presumably indexable via default behaviour, the absence of an explicit 'index, follow' directive is a minor hygiene gap, especially for a high-value event landing page.
findings.recommendation: Add <meta name='robots' content='index, follow'> to the <head> to make crawl intent explicit.
findings.fix_prompt: Add the following tag inside the <head> element: <meta name='robots' content='index, follow'>.

findings.issue: og:type is set to 'website' rather than a more specific type. While Open Graph does not have a native 'event' type, using 'website' misses an opportunity; for social sharing of event pages some platforms recognise custom namespaced types.
findings.recommendation: This is low priority; if the platform supports it, consider switching to og:type 'event' using the events Open Graph namespace. Otherwise, retain 'website' as a safe fallback.
findings.fix_prompt: If the publishing platform supports the Open Graph events namespace, update og:type to reference an event type. If not, this item can be left as 'website' and deprioritised.
